You speak when you see one of these things. Each has happened in this
project before.

- A patch where a fix was needed. The code gets a special case, a default on
  a path "that cannot happen", or a hand-written substitute for something the
  shared types or the kernel lack. (Before: 19 constructors written by hand
  outside the construct library, because the library could not hold calls.)
  What is missing is to be reported as missing, not filled in.

  deferred or called a first step; or the work goes into something the plan
  does not name. (Before: a night spent on the prover; the debugger and
  liveness never built.)
- The check made to pass instead of the work. A case or test weakened,
  removed, marked expected-red or re-pinned to the new output; an expected
  value copied from what the code computes; a verdict hard-coded.
- A second copy beside what exists. A second evaluator, encoder, name

  tshow written nine times; a second name resolution beside Judge.Scope.)
- Circles. The same failing check run again with nothing changed that could
  matter; another run where reading what is already there would answer.

  the vault or the code says it.
- A design question decided by the implementer. Something the plan or the
  design does not fix, or says differently, chosen and built on without
  being raised. (Before: integer counts through bv2nat where exact width was
  agreed.)
- A report that says more than happened. "Green" with something red,
  "proved" from links still open, "done" without the output read.

What each change serves:
# REVIEW I-061 3bc9e4502: 3 points

Read from `git show 3bc9e4502` (not the working tree). Standard: stride scheduling (Waldspurger–Weihl 1995): the pass picks who runs, the turn is a quantum charged by use; the lag bound is "least pass picked, one turn past it".

What holds: the new levelGrant is the classic form and removes ceilDiv with its last use. The homogeneity is right for weights below 1: StrideKeeps is degree 1 in (w_i, w_j) in each term, so scaling every weight by the common denominator D (ClassAnswers/ClassAnswersAt) leaves it unchanged. The derivation w_i x_j <= w_j W_i + w_i (q+m) is sound for a plain pick: j picked only while pass_j <= pass_i <= W_i/w_i (passFrom only raises j's pass, so x_j <= w_j(pass_j - passFrom_j) before its last turn), plus its last turn's work <= q+m. levinSum's induction (Levin.agda ~85-105) is real arithmetic, and the regrouping with d = q+m is correct. Old readers in ClassBound, Restarts (header + PausedBound + thm), Levin (header, StrideKeeps, LevinBound), StrideTree (levelGrant arity) and the Algorithm/Levin prose are all updated.

## 1. The awaited preference is not in the statement (Stride.agda urgentPass/goesFirst, ~l.84-92; Levin.agda StrideKeeps l.~62)
`chosenBy` orders by `urgentPass`: an awaited child reads a quantum LESS (`pass - q`). So j is picked while pass_j - q <= pass_i, i.e. pass_j <= pass_i + q, and x_j <= w_j (W_i/w_i + q) + (q+m). The invariant then needs the old `w_j q` term back: w_i x_j <= w_j W_i + w_i (w_j q + q + m). The new header says j "is picked only while its pass is at most i's"; that is false whenever j is awaited. The old statement covered this by accident (its w_j q was "within a quantum of i's pass"); dropping it with the distance-based grant removed the one place it was visible. Right shape: either state the awaited lead explicitly (term w_j q, or q in pass units, which in work is w_j q) or prove the bound is not needed (awaited only ever breaks ties among the same level...). Pick one and say it in the header; the statement must be true of `chosenBy`, not of a plain least-pass pick.

## 2. A doubled grant is not within q + m (Stride.agda levelGrant l.~104; Levin.agda header, StrideKeeps)
levelGrant = `doubling q (stalledOf t)` is `max q (2 * stalled)`, and a non-parkable check stopped at its grant g reports stalled = g (+ up to m), so its next turn is ~2g: 2q, 4q, ... The turn's work is then up to 2^k q, not q+m. The header's "and m then bounds that stop's work too" does not follow: m is a per-chunk granularity, not a bound on the doubled grant. The restated `(q + m)` is therefore true only for runnables that are parked (never report a stop). This was already so before, but the old grant took `min q ...` first so the doubling looked secondary; now the grant is "doubling q" and the bug is the headline. Right shape: make the premise explicit. Either (a) StrideKeeps' q is the largest grant any turn got (a parameter of the stretch, with doubling giving log2(U/q)+1 stops: the existing claim), or (b) the bound is stated for parked runnables and a separate term (the sum of the doubled turns, <= 2U + m per non-parkable check) carries the others. As written, LevinBound/PausedBound/ClassAnswers hold of an object (StrideKeeps) that the scheduler does not establish for non-parkable checks.

## 3. StrideKeeps is still a hypothesis; the acceptance asked for it proved
Item acceptance: "StrideKeeps restated/proved for the new grant". The commit restates it and re-proves only levinSum (a sum over the hypothesis). `git grep StrideKeeps` shows it used only in Levin/ClassBound/Restarts; nothing derives it from pickIn/chosenBy/levelGrant/chargedBy. So points 1 and 2 are exactly what the missing lemma would have caught, and the "weights below 1 and margin per turn" check orch asked for is only done on paper (the commit message). The lemma to state: for a trace of pick/charge steps with i eligible throughout, every j that ran satisfies the inequality; its proof is the three facts above (urgentPass lead, grant <= q' (point 2), natDiv/natMod carry exact in chargedBy so pass is work/w exactly). If this is deliberately left as the "named lower step" then the item must say so and the acceptance be changed; do not leave "proved" standing.

## Smaller (same point of correctness, not style)
- packages/tovrin-checker/src/Checker/Smt.hs:~2976 comment: "its next grant is its share's alone, never doubled" - the grant is no longer a share (it is the quantum); say "the quantum".
- Stride.agda header l.~27 "a runnable's work stays within a quantum and the meter's granularity of its share" is the same overclaim as 1-2 until they are fixed.

Give the file and line or the sentence that shows it, and what the
implementer should do instead, in at most five sentences.
